images.img2Desc: A man and a woman ride bicycles slowly along a quiet street. Both wear casual clothes and hats, and the woman has a basket on her bike. There are houses and parked cars behind them.

questions.prompt: What do you do in your free time?
questions.sampleA2:
I like to read books in my free time.

And I watch TV.

Sometimes I go to the park because it is nice.
questions.sampleB1:
In my free time, I enjoy reading. I think it's very relaxing.

I also like to watch movies, especially comedies.

Sometimes I meet my friends, and we go out for dinner. That's fun!
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, my free time is pretty precious, so I always try to make the most of it. I usually wind down by listening to music or going for a long walk to clear my head. When I get the chance, I love to catch up with friends over coffee. At the end of the day, I just like to strike a balance.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Bo'sh vaqtimda kitob o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman.

Va televizor ko'raman.

Ba'zan bog'ga boraman, chunki u yer yoqimli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Bo'sh vaqtimda kitob o'qishni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, bu juda dam beradi.

Shuningdek, kino ko'rishni ham yaxshi ko'raman, ayniqsa komediyalarni.

Ba'zida do'stlarim bilan uchrashaman va biz kechki ovqatga chiqamiz. Bu juda qiziqarli!
questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, bo'sh vaqtimda men dam olishimga va stressdan xalos bo'lishimga yordam beradigan mashg'ulotlar bilan shug'ullanishga harakat qilaman.

Mening eng sevimli mashg'ulotlarimdan biri bu musiqa tinglash, ko'pincha sayr qilish paytida.

Men ovqat pishirishni ham yaxshi ko'raman; yangi retseptlar bilan tajriba o'tkazish juda terapevtik.

Agar vaqtim ko'proq bo'lsa, men muzey yoki san'at galereyasiga tashrif buyurishim mumkin, chunki turli xil nuqtai nazarlarni ko'rish meni rag'batlantiradi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - What do you do in your free time?
idioms: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy - "Faqat ish qilish odamni zerikarli qiladi"
kill two birds with one stone - "bir tosh bilan ikki qushni urmoq"
phrases: unwind after a long day - "uzoq kundan keyin dam olmoq"
sentenceStarters: "In my free time, I usually..." - "Bo'sh vaqtimda, men odatda..."
"I'm particularly fond of..." - "Men ayniqsa ... ni yaxshi ko'raman"
"One of my favorite pastimes is..." - "Sevimli mashg'ulotlarimdan biri..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In my free time, I usually pursue a variety of hobbies to unwind after a long day. I'm particularly fond of reading fiction novels, as they allow me to escape into different worlds.
Additionally, I enjoy going for walks in the park, which helps me recharge my batteries both mentally and physically. On weekends, I sometimes meet up with friends for coffee or watch movies together.
As they say, "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy" – so I make sure to strike a balance between work and leisure.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bo'sh vaqtimda, uzoq kundan keyin dam olish uchun odatda turli xil sevimli mashg'ulotlar bilan shug'ullanaman. Men ayniqsa badiiy romanlarni o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki ular menga turli olamlarga qochishga imkon beradi.

Bundan tashqari, parkda sayr qilishni yoqtiraman, bu menga ham ruhiy, ham jismoniy jihatdan kuch yig'ishga yordam beradi. Dam olish kunlari ba'zan do'stlarim bilan qahva ichish uchun uchrashaman yoki birga kino ko'ramiz.

Aytishlaricha, "Faqat ish bilan mashg'ul bo'lish va o'yin-kulgi qilmaslik odamni zerikarli qilib qo'yadi" – shuning uchun men ish va dam olish o'rtasida muvozanatni saqlashga harakat qilaman.

I'm a bit of a bookworm, to be honest, and I mostly go for crime novels and biographies. The thing is, a real page-turner can keep me hooked until well past midnight.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you enjoy reading?
idioms: A reader lives a thousand lives - "Kitobxon ming hayot yashaydi"
don't judge a book by its cover - "kitobni muqovasiga qarab baholamaslik"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I absolutely love reading..." - "Ha, men o'qishni juda yaxshi ko'raman..."
"I'd consider myself an avid reader..." - "O'zimni kitobxon deb hisoblayman..."
"Reading allows me to..." - "O'qish menga ... imkonini beradi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I absolutely love reading! I'd consider myself an avid reader who enjoys various genres, from mystery novels to self-help books.
Reading allows me to broaden my horizons and learn about different cultures and perspectives. There's something incredibly relaxing about immersing myself in a captivating story after a busy day.
As they say, "A reader lives a thousand lives before he dies" – I genuinely believe that books open doors to endless possibilities and knowledge.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men kitob o'qishni juda yaxshi ko'raman! Men o'zimni turli janrlarni, jumladan, detektiv romanlardan tortib o'z-o'ziga yordam beruvchi kitoblarni yoqtiradigan ishtiyoqli kitobxon deb hisoblayman.

Kitob o'qish menga ufqlarimni kengaytirishga va turli madaniyatlar va nuqtai nazarlar haqida bilib olishga imkon beradi. Band kundan keyin o'zimni hayratlanarli hikoyaga berib yuborishda nihoyatda taskin beruvchi narsa bor.

Aytishlaricha, "Kitobxon o'lmasdan oldin mingta hayot kechiradi" – men chin dildan kitoblar cheksiz imkoniyatlar va bilimlar eshiklarini ochadi deb ishonaman.

questions.prompt: Do you read or write stories or poems?
questions.sampleA1: I read stories. I like stories. I no write.
questions.sampleA2: I read stories. I like to read stories before bed. But I don't write stories because it is hard.
questions.sampleB1: I like to read stories, especially fiction. I don't usually write stories or poems myself. However, I sometimes write in a journal. In my opinion, reading is more fun than writing because it's easier to relax.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I'd say I'm much more of a reader than a writer. I get through quite a few novels, but writing doesn't really come naturally to me. That said, I do jot down the odd idea in a journal now and then. I suppose I really admire people who can put their feelings into words like that; poetry is a real talent.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men hikoyalar o'qiyman. Menga hikoyalar yoqadi. Men yozmayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men hikoyalar o'qiyman. Yotishdan oldin hikoyalar o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman. Lekin men hikoyalar yozmayman, chunki bu qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men hikoyalar o'qishni yaxshi ko'raman, ayniqsa fantastikani. O'zim odatda hikoyalar yoki she'rlar yozmayman. Biroq, ba'zida kundalik yozaman. Mening fikrimcha, o'qish yozishdan ko'ra qiziqarliroq, chunki dam olish osonroq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men asosan hikoyalar o'qiyman, garchi ba'zan yozish bilan ham shug'ullanib turaman. Badiiy adabiyot o'qishni juda taskin beruvchi deb bilaman va bu dam olishning yaxshi usuli. Men ko'pincha hikoyalar yoki she'rlar yozmayman, lekin vaqti-vaqti bilan fikrlar yoki mulohazalarni yozib boradigan kundaligim bor. Men buni ko'proq qilishni xohlardim, lekin vaqt topish juda kamdan-kam hollarda nasib qiladi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you read or write stories or poems?
idioms: The pen is mightier than the sword - "Qalam qilichdan kuchli"
sentenceStarters: "I mainly read stories rather than..." - "Men asosan hikoyalarni yozishdan ko'ra o'qiyman..."
"I occasionally jot down..." - "Men ba'zan yozib qo'yaman..."
"I appreciate reading poems but..." - "She'rlarni o'qishni qadrlayman, lekin..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I mainly read stories rather than write them. I find reading fiction quite therapeutic and enjoyable – it helps me escape from reality for a while.
However, I occasionally jot down my thoughts in a journal, which is a form of creative writing, I suppose. As for poems, I appreciate reading them but I've never really tried writing poetry myself.
I admire people who can express themselves through literary works like that. As they say, "The pen is mightier than the sword" – words have incredible power.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men asosan hikoyalar o'qiyman, yozishdan ko'ra. Badiiy adabiyot o'qishni juda foydali va yoqimli deb bilaman – bu menga bir muddatga haqiqatdan qochishga yordam beradi.

Biroq, men vaqti-vaqti bilan o'z fikrlarimni kundalikka yozib boraman, bu ijodiy yozuvning bir shakli deb o'ylayman. She'rlarga kelsak, ularni o'qishni qadrlayman, lekin hech qachon o'zim she'r yozishga urinmaganman.

Men o'zini shunday adabiy asarlar orqali ifoda eta oladigan odamlarga qoyil qolaman. Aytishlaricha, "Qalam qilichdan kuchliroq" – so'zlar aql bovar qilmas kuchga ega.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see picture. Two girls. They eat. And trees.

I see two men. They bike.
questions.sampleA2:
In the pictures, I see friends.

One picture has girls. They are camping and eating. It is nice.

The other picture has boys. They are riding bikes and talking. It is good to be with friends because it is fun.
questions.sampleB1:
In the first picture, I can see two women. They are camping, I think. They are eating breakfast together.

In the second picture, there are two men. They are riding their bikes. Maybe they are friends too.

I think it's nice to spend time with friends like this. For example, going camping or riding bikes together is fun.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can clearly see two young women having breakfast at a picnic table in what appears to be a campsite. They’re enjoying bowls of cereal and fruit, with tents visible in the background, suggesting they’re on a camping trip and looking relaxed. Moving on to the second image, it shows a man and a woman out for a bike ride on a sunny street, likely in a residential area. They’re smiling and looking at each other, which implies they’re enjoying each other's company. Both images depict people engaging in outdoor activities and sharing pleasant moments. However, the first focuses on a morning meal in nature, whereas the second captures a leisurely journey through a town.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men rasm ko'ryapman. Ikki qiz. Ular ovqat yeyishyapti. Va daraxtlar.

Men ikki erkakni ko'ryapman. Ular velosipedda ketyapti.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Rasmlarda men do'stlarni ko'ryapman.

Bir rasmda qizlar bor. Ular chodirda dam olishyapti va ovqat yeyishyapti. Bu yaxshi.

Boshqa rasmda o'g'il bolalar bor. Ular velosipedda uchishyapti va gaplashishyapti. Do'stlar bilan birga bo'lish yaxshi, chunki bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda men ikki ayolni ko'ryapman. Ular chodirda dam olishyapti, deb o'ylayman. Ular birgalikda nonushta qilishyapti.

Ikkinchi rasmda ikki erkak bor. Ular velosipedda sayr qilishyapti. Ehtimol, ular ham do'stlardir.

O'ylashimcha, do'stlar bilan shunday vaqt o'tkazish yaxshi. Masalan, chodirda dam olishga borish yoki birgalikda velosipedda sayr qilish qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda lagerda bo'lib turgan ikki ayolni ko'rish mumkin. Ular stolda o'tirishibdi, ehtimol birgalikda ovqatlanishmoqda va juda xotirjam ko'rinishadi.

Ikkinchi rasmda velosipedda ketayotgan ikki erkak tasvirlangan. Ular bir-biriga qarashib turishibdi, bu ularning suhbatlashayotganini ko'rsatadi.

Ikkala rasm ham do'stlik va birgalikdagi mashg'ulotlar mavzusini aks ettiradi. Ular odamlarning qanday qilib bog'lanishi va ochiq havoda birgalikda vaqt o'tkazishdan zavqlanishi mumkinligini ta'kidlaydi. Ularning vaqti chog' o'tayotganga o'xshaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: A friend in need is a friend indeed - "Og'ir kunda do'st bilinadi"
birds of a feather flock together - "o'xshashlar birga yig'iladi"
sentenceStarters: "In these pictures, I can see..." - "Bu rasmlarda men ... ni ko'ryapman"
"In the first image, there are..." - "Birinchi rasmda ... bor"
"Both images show..." - "Ikkala rasm ham ... ni ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In these two pictures, I can see different ways friends spend quality time together.
In the first image, there are two young women at what appears to be a campsite. They're sitting at a wooden table having breakfast or a meal together, surrounded by tents and trees. They seem to be enjoying a casual conversation in a peaceful outdoor setting. The atmosphere looks incredibly relaxed and natural.
In the second picture, I can see two men cycling together on a quiet street. They're facing each other, possibly having stopped to chat. Both images show friends bonding through shared activities, whether it's camping or cycling.
As they say, "A friend in need is a friend indeed" – these pictures show the importance of nurturing friendships through shared experiences.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda do'stlar birgalikda sifatli vaqt o'tkazishning turli usullarini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi suratda, xuddi lagerga o'xshash joyda ikki yosh ayolni ko'rish mumkin. Ular yog'och stol atrofida o'tirib, nonushta qilishmoqda yoki birga ovqatlanishmoqda, atrofida chodirlar va daraxtlar bor. Ular tinch tabiat qo'ynida bemalol suhbatlashayotganga o'xshaydi. Atmosfera juda ham xotirjam va tabiiy ko'rinadi.

Ikkinchi suratda esa, ikki erkakning tinch ko'chada birga velosipedda ketayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Ular bir-biriga qarab turishibdi, ehtimol gaplashish uchun to'xtashgandir. Ikkala surat ham do'stlarning umumiy mashg'ulotlar orqali, xoh u lager bo'lsin, xoh velosipedda sayr qilish orqali, bir-birlari bilan yaqinlashayotganini ko'rsatadi.

Aytishlaricha, "Do'st og'ir kunda bilinadi" – bu suratlar do'stlikni umumiy tajribalar orqali mustahkamlash muhimligini ko'rsatadi.

questions.prompt: How do people in your country usually make friends?
questions.sampleA1: I go to school. I play with friends. We are happy.
questions.sampleA2: I meet friends at school. We play games. And we talk. Sometimes we go to the park together because it is fun.
questions.sampleB1: In my country, people usually make friends at school or at work. I think it's easier to make friends when you have something in common, like a class or a job. For example, I met my best friend in my English class. Also, some people meet friends through their hobbies, like sports or music.
questions.sampleB2: Well, in my country most friendships tend to start off at school or university, since you naturally bond over the same classes and struggles. A lot of people also hit it off at work or through mutual friends at family gatherings. To be honest, neighbours matter too; it's quite common to just strike up a conversation in the mahalla and take it from there.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men maktabga boraman. Men do'stlarim bilan o'ynayman. Biz baxtlimiz.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'stlarimni maktabda uchrataman. Biz o'yinlar o'ynaymiz. Va biz gaplashamiz. Ba'zan biz birga parkga boramiz, chunki bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB1: Mening mamlakatimda odamlar odatda maktabda yoki ishda do'st orttirishadi. Menimcha, bir xil narsangiz bo'lsa, do'st orttirish osonroq, masalan, dars yoki ish. Masalan, men eng yaxshi do'stimni ingliz tili darsimda uchratganman. Shuningdek, ba'zi odamlar o'zlarining sevimli mashg'ulotlari orqali do'stlashadilar, masalan, sport yoki musiqa.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, mening mamlakatimda odamlar do'stlashishining bir nechta keng tarqalgan usullari bor. Eng tipik yo'llardan biri bu ta'lim muassasalari orqali, boshlang'ich maktab, universitet yoki hatto kattalar uchun ta'lim kurslari bo'ladimi, farqi yo'q. Umumiy tajribalar va hamkorlikdagi loyihalar aloqalarni tabiiy ravishda rivojlantiradi. Yana bir muhim yo'nalish - bu ish joyi; hamkasblar ko'pincha umumiy qiyinchiliklar va maqsadlar tufayli birlashadilar. Bundan tashqari, sport klublari yoki ko'ngillilar tashkilotlari kabi jamoat tadbirlarida ishtirok etish sizni fikrlash doirasi bir xil bo'lgan odamlar bilan tanishtirishi mumkin. Garchi, bu odamga va uning turmush tarziga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - How do people in your country usually make friends?
idioms: No man is an island - "Hech kim yolg'iz orol emas"
sentenceStarters: "In my country, people typically..." - "Mening mamlakatimda odamlar odatda..."
"The most common way is through..." - "Eng keng tarqalgan usul..."
"Additionally, many people meet through..." - "Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik ... orqali tanishadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In my country, people typically make friends through various social settings.
The most common way is through school or university, where young people naturally form friendships with classmates who share common interests. Workplaces are also important for adults to expand their social circles.
Additionally, many people meet through mutual friends at gatherings or celebrations. In traditional communities, neighbourhood connections remain strong, and people often strike up conversations with their neighbors.
Recently, joining clubs or sports teams has become popular for meeting like-minded individuals. As they say, "No man is an island" – we all need social connections.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening mamlakatimda odamlar odatda turli ijtimoiy muhitlar orqali do'st orttirishadi.

Eng keng tarqalgan usul - bu maktab yoki universitet, bu yerda yoshlar o'z sinfdoshlari bilan umumiy qiziqishlarga ega bo'lgan holda tabiiy ravishda do'stlashadilar. Ish joylari ham kattalar uchun o'z ijtimoiy doiralarini kengaytirish uchun muhimdir.

Bundan tashqari, ko'p odamlar yig'ilishlar yoki bayramlarda o'zaro do'stlar orqali tanishadilar. An'anaviy jamoalarda mahalliy aloqalar kuchli bo'lib qolmoqda va odamlar ko'pincha qo'shnilari bilan suhbatlashib ketishadi.

Yaqinda klublarga yoki sport jamoalariga qo'shilish o'xshash fikrlaydigan odamlar bilan tanishish uchun mashhur bo'lib ketdi. Aytishlaricha, "Hech kim orol emas" - hammamizga ijtimoiy aloqalar kerak.

questions.prompt: What do you think of making friends on the internet?
questions.sampleA1: I like internet. I have friends. They are nice.
questions.sampleA2: I think it's good. I can talk to people online. And I have friends from other countries. But I don't know them in real life.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think making friends online can be good. For example, you can meet people who like the same things as you. However, it's also important to be careful. You don't always know who people really are online, so you should be cautious.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I have mixed feelings about it. On the plus side, the internet lets you bridge the distance and meet like-minded people from all over the world. The thing is, you can never be sure who's on the other end, so fake profiles are a worry. I suppose online friendships can be real, but I'd still take them with a pinch of salt.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga internet yoqadi. Mening do'stlarim bor. Ular yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, bu yaxshi. Men internetda odamlar bilan gaplasha olaman. Va menda boshqa davlatlardan do'stlarim bor. Lekin men ularni hayotda tanimayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha internetda do'st orttirish yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin.
Misol uchun, siz o'zingizga o'xshash narsalarni yoqtiradigan odamlar bilan tanishishingiz mumkin.
Biroq, ehtiyot bo'lish ham muhim. Siz har doim odamlarning internetda kim ekanligini bilmaysiz, shuning uchun hushyor bo'lishingiz kerak.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Internetda do'st orttirish haqida men aralash his-tuyg'ularga egaman. Bir tomondan, u o'ziga xos qiziqishlarga ega bo'lgan yoki uzoqda yashovchi odamlar bilan bog'lanish imkoniyatini beradi, bu esa sizning dunyoqarashingizni kengaytirishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, onlayn hamjamiyatlar juda qo'llab-quvvatlovchi bo'lishi mumkin.

Biroq, soxta profillar yoki yuzma-yuz muloqotdan kelib chiqadigan haqiqiy aloqaning yo'qligi kabi potentsial xavflardan xabardor bo'lish juda muhim. Shuning uchun, onlayn do'stlik qimmatli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, ma'lum darajada shubha zarur.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - What do you think of making friends on the internet?
idioms: All that glitters is not gold - "Yaltiraganining hammasi oltin emas"
take with a grain of salt - "shubha bilan qabul qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I think making friends online has..." - "Internetda do'stlashish ... deb o'ylayman"
"On the positive side..." - "Ijobiy tomoni..."
"However, there are concerns about..." - "Biroq, ... haqida tashvishlar bor"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I think making friends on the internet has both advantages and disadvantages.
On the positive side, it allows people to bridge geographical gaps and connect with others who share similar interests, regardless of location. Social media and online communities can help introverted people feel more comfortable expressing themselves.
However, there are significant concerns about online friendships. It's difficult to verify someone's true identity, and cases of catfishing are quite common. Virtual interactions can never fully replace face-to-face communication.
Overall, I believe online friendships can be genuine connections, but people should exercise caution. As they say, "All that glitters is not gold" – things online aren't always what they seem.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, internetda do'st orttirishning ham afzalliklari, ham kamchiliklari bor.

Ijobiy tomoni shundaki, u odamlarga geografik to'siqlarni yengib o'tishga va joylashuvidan qat'i nazar, o'xshash qiziqishlarga ega bo'lgan boshqalar bilan bog'lanishga imkon beradi. Ijtimoiy media va onlayn hamjamiyatlar tortinchoq odamlarga o'zlarini ifoda etishda o'zlarini qulayroq his qilishlariga yordam berishi mumkin.

Biroq, onlayn do'stliklar haqida jiddiy xavotirlar mavjud. Kimningdir haqiqiy shaxsini tekshirish qiyin va "katislik" holatlari juda keng tarqalgan. Virtual muloqotlar hech qachon yuzma-yuz muloqotni to'liq almashtira olmaydi.

Umuman olganda, menimcha, onlayn do'stliklar chinakam aloqalar bo'lishi mumkin, lekin odamlar ehtiyot bo'lishlari kerak. Aytishlaricha, "Yaltiroqning hammasi ham oltin emas" - onlayndagi narsalar har doim ham ko'ringanidek bo'lmaydi.

questions.sampleB1:
I think teachers are very important.

In my opinion, they should be paid more money because their job is hard.

Also, schools need more money to buy new books and computers.

For example, my school doesn't have enough computers.

I think children learn quickly, but adults can learn too if they try.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so this is a topic I feel pretty strongly about, actually. To start with the question of pay, no, I honestly don't think teachers are paid anywhere near enough. When you think about it, they're the ones shaping future generations, yet in a lot of countries teaching is an undervalued profession. The thing is, if the salary doesn't reflect the workload, you end up driving away talented people who'd otherwise stay, and that's a real shame. A well-paid teacher is a motivated teacher, after all. Moving on to funding, yes, I'd definitely say my country should pump more money into schools. A lot of buildings are falling apart, and classes are often overcrowded. To be honest, if the government were to invest in better facilities, modern equipment and smaller class sizes, it would pay off in the long run. Education is basically the backbone of any economy, so it's money well spent. You simply can't cut corners when it comes to a child's future. As for whether it's easier to learn as a child or an adult, I suppose it cuts both ways. Children are like sponges; they pick things up incredibly fast, especially languages. They soak up new information almost without trying. That said, adults bring a lot to the table too: they've got more discipline, life experience and stronger critical thinking. So at the end of the day, I'd say it depends on what you're actually trying to learn. Either way, you're never too old to learn something new.

questions.sampleAnswer:
These are important questions about education.
Firstly, regarding teacher salaries, I don't think teachers are paid enough in most countries, including mine. Teaching is often an undervalued profession despite its crucial role in shaping future generations. Teachers deserve adequate compensation for their dedication.
Secondly, I strongly believe my country should allocate more funds to schools. Better educational infrastructure, updated learning materials, and smaller class sizes would significantly improve the quality of education.
Lastly, children generally find it easier to learn new things because their brains can absorb information quickly. However, adults have advantages too, such as better focus and motivation. As they say, "You're never too old to learn".

questions.prompt: Should laptops be allowed in classrooms?
questions.sampleA1: Laptop? Yes. I like laptop. School is good.
questions.sampleA2: I think laptops are good. Because I can write. And I can look things up. But sometimes I play games. So, maybe not always good.
questions.sampleB1: I think laptops in classrooms can be useful. For example, we can use them to take notes and do research. However, some students might get distracted and use them for other things, like social media. So, there are good and bad things. I think it depends on the student.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is one of those questions that really splits opinion, so let me look at both sides. On the one hand, there's a strong case for allowing laptops. For a start, they give students instant access to a wealth of information, so they can look things up on the spot instead of waiting. They also make group work far smoother; tools like shared documents let everyone chip in at once. On top of that, getting comfortable with technology builds up the kind of digital skills that employers are crying out for these days. In many ways, a laptop can turn a passive lesson into something far more interactive. On the other hand, I can completely see why some teachers are against it. The biggest issue, to be honest, is distraction. It's all too easy for a student to drift off onto social media or games the moment the lesson gets a bit dull. There's also the temptation to copy and paste rather than actually thinking things through, which can undermine academic honesty. And let's face it, a screen can put a real barrier between the teacher and the class. At the end of the day, though, I don't think banning them outright is the answer. My view is that a happy medium works best: let students use laptops for specific tasks, but with clear ground rules and a bit of monitoring. That way, you get the best of both worlds without letting things get out of hand. As they say, everything in moderation.

vocabulary.title: Q8 - Should laptops be allowed in classrooms?

for: Laptops can be a useful tool in the classroom and can enhance learning.
Laptops can be used to facilitate collaboration and group work in the classroom.
Laptops can be used to access online resources in the classroom.
against: Laptops can be a distraction in classrooms and impede learning.
Laptops can be a source of disruption in classrooms and lead to an increase in cheating.
Laptops can be a source of security risks in classrooms.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a topic that generates considerable debate in educational circles. Let me present both perspectives.
Those who support laptops in classrooms argue that they can significantly enhance the learning experience. Laptops provide access to vast online educational resources, allowing students to research topics instantly. They also facilitate interactive learning through educational software and collaborative tools like Google Docs, which enable group projects. Moreover, using laptops helps students develop digital literacy skills essential for the modern workplace.
On the other hand, opponents raise valid concerns. Laptops can be major distractions, as students might browse social media or play games instead of paying attention. There are also concerns about academic integrity, as laptops make it easier to cheat or plagiarize. Additionally, cybersecurity risks are legitimate worries.
In my opinion, a balanced approach is best. Schools should allow laptops but implement clear guidelines and monitoring systems. As they say, "Everything in moderation".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ta’lim doiralarida ancha bahs-munozaralarga sabab bo‘ladigan mavzu. Keling, har ikki nuqtai nazarni taqdim etay.

Sinf xonalarida noutbuklarni qo‘llab-quvvatlovchilar, ular o‘quv jarayonini sezilarli darajada yaxshilashi mumkinligini ta’kidlaydilar. Noutbuklar talabalarga onlayn ta’lim resurslariga keng kirish imkoniyatini beradi, bu esa ularga mavzularni bir zumda o‘rganishga imkon beradi. Ular, shuningdek, ta’lim dasturlari va Google Docs kabi hamkorlik vositalari orqali interaktiv o‘qishni osonlashtiradi, bu esa guruh loyihalarini amalga oshirishga imkon beradi. Bundan tashqari, noutbuklardan foydalanish talabalarga zamonaviy ish joyi uchun zarur bo‘lgan raqamli savodxonlik ko‘nikmalarini rivojlantirishga yordam beradi.

Boshqa tomondan, qarshilar asosli xavotirlarni keltirib chiqaradilar. Noutbuklar asosiy chalg'ituvchi omil bo'lishi mumkin, chunki talabalar diqqatni qaratish o'rniga ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni ko'rib chiqishi yoki o'yinlar o'ynashi mumkin. Shuningdek, akademik halollik borasida ham xavotirlar mavjud, chunki noutbuklar aldash yoki plagiat qilishni osonlashtiradi. Bundan tashqari, kiberxavfsizlik xavflari qonuniy tashvishlardir.

Mening fikrimcha, muvozanatli yondashuv eng yaxshisidir. Maktablar noutbuklarga ruxsat berishi kerak, lekin aniq ko'rsatmalar va monitoring tizimlarini joriy qilishi kerak. Aytganlaridek, "Har narsada me'yor bo'lishi kerak".
